generic_sampling_rules.int: Sample integer uniformly within the column's semantic range (or [min,max] of the column when no range rule exists); 5-30% NULL when nullable; never NULL for primary keys.
generic_sampling_rules.text: Sample from a short pool of distinct values; 20-50% near-duplicate variants (case, trailing space, one extra char); 5-30% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.date: Sample date in ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD; 5-30% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary: Include values at each literal boundary and one step on each side (ints +/-1, dates +/-1 day, text case variants and near-duplicate strings), clamped to the column's semantic range so no injected value violates a declared formula.
generic_sampling_rules.near_variant: For each LIKE literal, generate the exact literal and a near variant (e.g. '%Mik%' for '%Mike%').
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates_for_distinct: For DISTINCT columns, ensure 20-50% of rows share a value with another row.
generic_sampling_rules.tie: For ORDER columns, ensure at least one tie at the minimum rank.
generic_sampling_rules.null: For nullable columns, include a NULL share (5-30%) and at least one NULL row per column per instance; nullable foreign keys with an unmatched_join_rows target also get at least one NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh: Fresh values are generated from the pool; no reuse of original values.

semantic_rules_and_formulas.formula: mID IS NULL OR mID IN (SELECT mID FROM Movie)
rID IS NULL OR rID IN (SELECT rID FROM Reviewer)

supporting_evidence: Rating.stars BETWEEN 1 AND 5 holds on all shown rows (2,3,4,5)
Movie.year BETWEEN 1900 AND 2025 holds on all shown rows (1937-2009)
Rating.ratingDate >= '2000-01-01' holds on all non-NULL shown rows (2011-01-09..2011-01-30)
uncertainty: No formula for Movie.title; it is a free text.
No formula for Reviewer.name; it is a free text.
No formula for Movie.director beyond non-empty text; it is a free text.
Rating.stars boundary value 6 dropped because it violates stars BETWEEN 1 AND 5.
Rating.mID and Rating.rID are nullable FKs; NULL child FKs are planted to realise unmatched_join_rows.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows `rows_added: 0` and `rows_skipped: 0` for all 20 instances, yet the nullable-column report shows generated rows (e.g. `Movie.director: generated rows: NULL 9 / 68`, `Rating.ratingDate: generated rows: NULL 34 / 280`). The CLI computes `added`/`skipped` from `_G['rows_added']`/`_G['rows_skipped']`, but `_one()` never populates these globals (it discards the dict returned by `write_instance_sqlite`), and in the multiprocessing path `_G` in the parent is never updated at all. So the reported `rows_added`/`rows_skipped` are always 0 regardless of what was written. This is a reporting bug, not a data bug, but it makes the execution feedback unreliable for verifying that generated rows were actually appended.
issues.requested_revision: Have `_one()` return/aggregate the `rows_ok`/`rows_failed` dict from `write_instance_sqlite` (e.g. via a per-worker accumulator returned alongside the status, or a shared counter), and report the true `rows_added`/`rows_skipped` in the CLI summary. Do not rely on module-level `_G` mutation in worker processes.

issues.evidence: `_fk_draw` (instance.py) is used for `Rating.mID` and `Rating.rID`. The NULL share passed is `_null_share(...) if not cm.notnull and cm.pk_pos == 0 else 0.0`. For `Rating.mID`/`Rating.rID` the compact share is 0 (feedback: `Rating.mID distinct: 6, null: 0`), and `_null_share` only forces a floor when `is_null_target(spec, ...)` is true. `Rating.mID`/`Rating.rID` are not in `null_targets` (only `Movie.director`, `Rating.ratingDate`), so `null_share` stays 0 and no NULL FK is ever planted. The spec's `unmatched_join_rows` target for `Rating.mID` explicitly requires `child_rows_with_null_fk: true`, and the interface NULL rule says every nullable column (including nullable FKs) must get at least one NULL row per instance. Feedback confirms `Rating.mID: generated rows: NULL 0 / 280` and `Rating.rID: generated rows: NULL 0 / 280`.
issues.requested_revision: For nullable FK columns that carry an `unmatched_join_rows` target (or generally for nullable FK columns), ensure at least one NULL FK value per instance and a NULL share following the compact share (with a floor when the compact share is 0 but the column is nullable and the spec requires null child FKs). Either add `Rating.mID`/`Rating.rID` to `null_targets` in the specification, or make `_fk_draw`/`build_random_instance` plant NULLs for nullable FK columns with `unmatched_join_rows`.

issues.evidence: The specification's `semantic_rules_and_formulas` contains `Movie.director: director IS NULL OR director = 1`. This is not a meaningful domain rule (director is free text; `director = 1` is a type-mismatched comparison) and is listed under `uncertainty` as "No formula for Movie.director; it is a free text." The program's `_int_range`/`parse_int_range` would not apply it to a text column, so it is inert, but it is a spurious rule that could mislead a reader into thinking director is constrained to the integer 1.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the `Movie.director` formula (or replace it with a genuine constraint such as `director IS NULL OR length(director) > 0`). Keep `Movie.director` as a free-text column with only the NULL-share and boundary/duplicate/group-size patterns.

issues.evidence: The specification's `uncertainty` lists `No formula for Rating.stars; it is a free integer` and `No formula for Movie.ratingDate; it is a free date`, but `semantic_rules_and_formulas` does contain `Rating.stars: stars BETWEEN 1 AND 5` and `Rating.ratingDate: ratingDate IS NULL OR ratingDate >= '2000-01-01'`. The uncertainty list is inconsistent with the formulas section. Also `Rating.stars` boundary targets include value 6 (`values: [3,4,5,6]`), which conflicts with the `stars BETWEEN 1 AND 5` formula; the program's `_boundary_values` will inject 6 into `Rating.stars`, producing values outside the declared domain.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the uncertainty list with the formulas section. For `Rating.stars`, either drop the boundary value 6 (since it violates `stars BETWEEN 1 AND 5`) or relax the formula; the program should not inject boundary values that violate a declared semantic formula. Similarly confirm `Rating.ratingDate` boundary handling respects `>= '2000-01-01'`.

issues.evidence: `_boundary_values` (instance.py) injects all `comparison_boundary` target values plus +/-1 for ints without checking them against the column's semantic formula. For `Rating.stars` the targets are `[3,4,5,6]`, so 6 (and 7 via +1) can be generated, violating `stars BETWEEN 1 AND 5`. For `Movie.year` targets `[1978,...,2001]` plus +/-1 give 1977 and 2002, which are within `1900..2025` so fine, but the general mechanism does not clamp boundary values to the formula range.
issues.requested_revision: In `_boundary_values` (or in the samplers), filter/clamp boundary values to the column's semantic formula range (e.g. `stars` in [1,5], `year` in [1900,2025]) so that injected boundary values never violate declared domain rules. Coordinate with the designer on whether 6 should remain a boundary target.

issues.evidence: `_group_cap` is applied to samplers *after* the generated columns are already sampled (`cols = {cm.name: [samplers[...].sample() ...]}` runs before the `_apply_group_cap` loop). The cap therefore has no effect on the current instance's generated values; it only affects later calls. As a result `group_sizes` / `duplicates_for_distinct` targets (e.g. `Movie.title`, `Reviewer.name`, `Movie.director`) are not actually realised by construction as the docstring claims.
issues.requested_revision: Apply `_apply_group_cap` to the samplers before sampling the generated columns (i.e. move the cap loop above the `cols = {...}` comprehension), so the distinct-value cap actually constrains the generated values and realises the group-size / duplicate-share targets.

issues.evidence: `_fk_draw` reserves parent values for "no children" by truncating the pool (`pool = pool[:max(1, len(pool) - 1)]`), but the parent's generated rows are drawn from `inst[pt][pc]` which includes compact + generated parent keys. Because `Rating` is built after `Movie`/`Reviewer` in `table_order`, this is fine for FK validity, but the `unmatched_join_rows` target also requires `parent_rows_without_children: true`. The truncation only removes one parent value from the draw pool; with the cycling `sizes` pattern it is not guaranteed that at least one parent row has zero children, and the feedback does not report parent-without-children counts. This is a weaker realisation than the spec target.
issues.requested_revision: Explicitly guarantee at least one parent row with no children (e.g. exclude a chosen parent key from the FK draw pool and verify it is not drawn), and add a check/report of parent rows without children to the execution feedback so the `unmatched_join_rows` target is verifiably realised.

unresolved_checks: The `rows_added`/`rows_skipped` counters are unreliable (always 0), so it cannot be confirmed from the summary alone that generated rows were appended; the nullable-column report and `construction_pairs` suggest they were, but the counter bug should be fixed to make this verifiable.
Whether `Rating.stars` boundary value 6 should be kept (conflicts with `stars BETWEEN 1 AND 5`) is a designer decision; the program currently injects it.
The `Movie.director` formula `director IS NULL OR director = 1` is inert in the program but is a spurious rule; its removal is requested but does not block generation.

`construction_pairs` reports 27/80 separated with no per-group breakdown (`construction_pairs_by_group` empty); a missing separation alone is not treated as a generation error per the instructions, but the empty breakdown limits diagnosis.

issues.evidence: Specification's supporting_evidence states 'Movie.title distinct: 8, duplicates: 0' and 'Reviewer.name distinct: 8, duplicates: 0', yet per_column_exceptions require duplicates_for_distinct (20-50% duplicate share) and group_sizes (1, 2, >=3) for both Movie.title and Reviewer.name. The compact data has no duplicates, so these targets are only realisable in generated rows.
issues.requested_revision: No change required for pass; note that duplicate/group-size targets for Movie.title and Reviewer.name are constructed in generated rows (via _group_cap capping distinct fresh values) rather than reflected in the compact data. If the intent was to describe the compact data, the supporting_evidence wording should be clarified.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows 'Movie.title: generated rows: NULL 0 / 68', 'Movie.year: NULL 0 / 68', 'Rating.stars: NULL 0 / 280', 'Reviewer.name: NULL 0 / 84'. These columns are nullable in the schema but are not in null_targets, and _null_share returns 0.0 for non-null-target columns with no compact NULLs. Per the interface NULL rule, this is noted but does not block a pass.
issues.requested_revision: Optional: if the interface NULL rule is to be applied to all nullable columns (not only null_targets), extend _null_share to give a small NULL share to nullable non-target columns. Not required for pass.

issues.evidence: construction_pairs: eligible 80, separated 31, unknown_executions 0. 49 pairs are not separated. This is expected given the compact-plus-append design and the fact that many boundary/duplicate targets are realised only probabilistically; a missing separation alone does not establish a generation error.
issues.requested_revision: No change required; separation is not a pass criterion per instructions.

unresolved_checks: Whether the 20-50% duplicate_share targets for Movie.title / Reviewer.name are actually met in generated rows was not directly measured; only group-size capping is applied. This is a soft target and does not block pass.

Whether ties_for_order_limit (tie at rank 1 on MIN/AVG(stars)) are realised in every instance was not directly verified; the _fk_draw distribution and stars sampler make ties likely but not guaranteed.
reviews.summary: The program ran cleanly (20/20 instances, 0 failures, reproducible), integrity constraints hold (0 FK/NOT NULL/PK violations), compact rows are preserved (writer copies the compact file and appends only generated rows), and dependencies are respected (FKs drawn from parent compact+generated values, NULLs planted for nullable FKs with unmatched_join_rows). Semantic formulas are enforced by construction: stars clamped to [1,5] (boundary 6 dropped per uncertainty note), year clamped to [1900,2025], ratingDate >= 2000-01-01, mID/rID in parent sets or NULL. Boundary values, LIKE literals, near variants, group-size caps, and NULL shares are implemented in the samplers. The specification is consistent with the schema and the program implements it; remaining gaps are soft/probabilistic targets that do not block a pass.
